title: Enforcement of Labour Court Orders on Errant Employers
what_it_is: Enforcement of Labour Court Orders on Errant Employers

sections.label: MOM mediation and Labour Court
sections.summary: Mediation by MOM and adjudication by the Labour Court resolved more than 95% of these claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Through mediation by MOM and adjudication by the Labour Court, we have been able to resolve more than 95% of these claims.

sections.label: Prosecutions and injured worker cases
sections.summary: In the last three years, 158 employers were prosecuted and convicted for salary-related offences, and in 2016 over 99.9% of about 16,000 injured workers had cases resolved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In the last three years, 158 employers have been prosecuted and convicted for salary-related offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In 2016, over 99.9% of the approximately 16,000 injured workers had their cases successfully resolved.

sections.label: Prosecutions for non-insurance
sections.summary: In the last five years, 14 employers were prosecuted for non-insurance and non-compensation or work injury.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In the last five years, 14 employers have been prosecuted for non-insurance and non-compensation or work injury.

sections.label: Assurance on insurance coverage
sections.summary: A Member asks whether MOM can assure insurance coverage for local and foreign employees and publicise actions for foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, for the upstream actions by MOM, is there a more certain way by which the Ministry can assure and ensure that the insurance coverage is for both local and foreign employees?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As it is, I think there seems to be a gap somewhere, where some of the employers did not have their workers covered and, therefore, some of the issues arose.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Looking at the comprehensive slew of measures that the Minister has described, I am not sure if many people know about them and so, is there a way by which MOM can facilitate and publicise a lot more on the actions that can be taken, especially for workers who are from foreign lands and who may not be clued in and where the language might be an issue?

sections.label: Seizing errant employers' assets
sections.summary: Ms Phua is asked to keep supplementary questions short, and errant employers have been told to go and seize assets.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: Ms Phua, please keep your supplementary questions short.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: They have been told to go and seize the assets of the errant employers.

sections.label: Problems among 16,000 cases
sections.summary: Out of the 16,000 cases, only five cases had problems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Out of the 16,000 cases, only five cases had problems.

sections.label: Employers prosecuted in five cases
sections.summary: All five employers in the five cases have been or are being prosecuted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: For the five cases, all of the five employers have been or are being prosecuted.

sections.label: Guaranteed minimum payment for workers
sections.summary: Every affected worker is guaranteed at least $3,000, comprising $2,000 partial payment from the employer and $1,000 from MWC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Every worker affected is guaranteed of at least $3,000; that is, $2,000 of partial payment from the employer and $1,000 from MWC.

sections.label: Resolution rate of cases
sections.summary: As a result, 95% of the cases were resolved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: As a result, we were able to resolve 95% of them.

sections.label: Debarment of directors for unpaid salaries
sections.summary: Directors blamed for non-payment of salaries face debarment that follows them to new companies until outstanding salaries are paid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For the cases where the businesses ceased operations and majority of them ceased operations, will the owners or the directors be allowed to start new businesses or take up directorships in other businesses while they continue to not pay the salaries that were owed to the workers that were approved by the Labour Court?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: This refers to directors who deserve blame for not paying salary, regardless of whether it is due to negligence, intentional or otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In other words, if you are a director of a company and you have contributed to the non-payment of salary, the debarment applies to this director as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: So, this director can go on to open and start a new company, the debarment will follow him to the new company until he pays up the outstanding salary to the ex-employees.

sections.label: Foreign workers owed unpaid salaries
sections.summary: Last year, 115 foreign workers were owed salaries that were unpaid and unresolved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Last year, 115 foreign workers were owed salaries, unpaid and unresolved.
